purpose: Append-only notebook for the COW synthesis loop. The loop runs unattended, so anything a human would want to know afterwards goes here instead of stopping the run: fidelity judgements worth a second opinion, tool flags the writer overrode, defects found in the source, and chapters the driver rejected.
how: Never hand-edit. Append with: python3 scripts/synthesis-note.py --book <book> --chapter <ch> --kind <kind> --note '<text>' [--verses 3,7]. Review with: python3 scripts/synthesis-note.py --list [--kind ...] [--since YYYY-MM-DD].

kinds.fidelity: why a verse was graded B, or an A that felt borderline
kinds.disagreement: a STRETCH / ENTITIES / UNSOURCED flag the writer judged a false positive, and why
kinds.source-defect: scrape residue, a misplaced witness block, an out-of-range verse key
kinds.rejected: written by the driver when a chapter fails verification and is reverted
kinds.observation: anything else the next reader should know

entries.note: Graded B: each leans on a Keil and Delitzsch or Matthew Henry block filed under a different verse key (K&D vv.10-13 resumption, Henry v9 on Mahanaim, K&D v37 distributive gloss). Faithful to the chapter's catena, not to the verse's own slot.

Every Jamieson, Fausset and Brown block in this chapter is scrape residue from elsewhere: Deuteronomy on lending, Exodus on the Hebrew servant, and repeated Passover/feast material. All omitted silently; JFB is named nowhere in the chapter.

Ellicott appears nowhere in this chapter's catena or corpora, yet the OLD prose named him on all 45 verses. This is the documented Joshua fabrication from the 2026-08-09 audit. Dropped entirely rather than re-grounded.
ENTITIES flags for Chronicler, Maccabean, Zebulunite judged false positives: my own descriptive nouns, and Maccabean is grounded since K&D cite 1 Macc 5:26 on Busra.
Expansion of 3x-8x on the thin verses is inherent to the thin exemption, which pairs a 20-30 word catena with a 120-word floor. Not evidence of invention.

First draft introduced facts absent from this catena: Deborah and Elijah at the Kishon, Jacob naming Mahanaim, Moses sending from the wilderness of Kedemoth, and a Numbers 35:6 citation. All removed before commit rather than recorded as B; an unsupported claim is a rewrite, not a note.

Graded B: v4 uses Henry's summer/winter detail from his block under verse 1; v10 uses K&D's Geder and Hormah identifications from the verse 8 block. Both grounded in the chapter, not in the verse's own slot.
Every Jamieson, Fausset and Brown block in this chapter is scrape residue on the covenant blessings and Psalm 144, foreign to Joshua 12. Omitted silently; JFB is named nowhere.
Ellicott appears nowhere in this chapter's catena or corpora. This is the second half of the documented Joshua fabrication (ch 12 and ch 21). Dropped entirely.

ENTITIES flags for Edomite, Jerome, Isaiah, Acts, Sidetes and Onomasticon are all false positives: inflections and spelling variants of source terms (Henry's Edom, Gill's Jerom, Clarke's Sydetes, K&D's Onom.) plus book names inside ref links that the detector cannot see.
STRETCH of 8.3x and 11.2x are inherent to the thin exemption: a 12-19 word catena against a 120-word floor. The prose stays inside what Gill supplies.

First draft brought in Gibeon and Caleb from Joshua 9, 10 and 14 - true facts, absent from this catena. Rewritten before commit rather than graded B. Same failure mode as joshua 21; it recurs on list chapters where the register itself says almost nothing.

BLOCKED, not attempted. Four verses measure over 200 raw source words so the validator refuses the thin exemption, but hold only 15-86 usable words once the Jamieson-Fausset-Brown scrape residue is dropped (Day of Atonement, the scapegoat, covering the blood of game - all Leviticus 16/17, foreign to Numbers 7). Writing them to the 350-word floor would be a 17x expansion of pure padding, which is the exact defect this repair effort exists to remove; marking them thin fails the validator's source check. There is no honest way to pass this chapter under the current contract.

Corpus-wide scan: 575 verses across 387 chapters have this shape - raw blob over 200 words, usable material under 200 once the noise block is dropped. Worst offenders psalms 78, ezekiel 23, numbers 31 (6 verses each). The two rules genuinely conflict: 'skip noise silently' tells the writer to ignore the residue, while the thin exemption measures the source WITH it. The fix is one line in validate-synthesis.py source_words(): measure after stripping the same noise the writer is required to ignore. That LOOSENS the exemption, so no committed chapter can break. Not changed unilaterally - the loop doc records the floor and the exemption as owner decisions.

Numbers 7 is also the largest unit in the corpus at 89 verses, 72 of them the repeated tribal offering with 12-21 words of source each. Even unblocked it is the chapter most likely to produce templated filler, and the anti-templating rule (Job 5 precedent) bites hardest here. Worth handling deliberately rather than as a routine queue item.

RESOLVED: owner approved the contract change. source_words now subtracts voice blocks declared on the tags entry as excluded_voices, so the thin exemption measures the source the way the writer is required to read it. Declared rather than auto-detected, and a declared voice must actually head a block in that verse's blob. numbers 7 vv 4/16/40/82 are now thin-eligible (18/84/13/13 usable words). Full corpus validator, quality gate, data and commentary validators all pass unchanged.

Pericope grouping landed 2026-08-10. A tags entry may carry range + pericope_label and stand for a span; prose is keyed at the span start. Where ranges are used the spans must tile the chapter exactly. Coverage is NOT enforced on chapters without ranges: a scan found 8 pre-existing gaps that are legitimate or historical - 2chronicles 27 (the documented out-of-range scrape key 16), galatians 2 (29) and 1corinthians 16 (55) are out-of-range keys correctly omitted; deuteronomy 14 (8,14), numbers 26 (60), numbers 29 (4,10,22,28,34) and numbers 34 (25) are in-range source keys with no synthesis; romans 16 carries a synthesis for v24 which the catena lacks. Worth a look, none caused by this change.

cow/numbers/7.json carries Jamieson, Fausset and Brown blocks that are Leviticus 16 Day-of-Atonement scrape residue (the scapegoat lots, the high priest's linen and pontifical dress, the sprinkling before the mercy seat) filed under vv. 4, 10, 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, 46, 52, 64 and 82. Declared as excluded_voices on every entry covering those keys; JFB is named nowhere in the chapter.

Rewritten as 19 pericope entries tiling all 89 verses: 1; 2-3; 4-5; 6-9; 10-11; then one entry per tribal day (12-17 ... 78-83); 84-88; 89. The twelve days are the case the pericope contract was built for — vv.18-83 are almost entirely 'See Gill on' stubs plus JFB residue, so ten of the twelve day entries take the thin exemption. Each day was given a distinct centre of gravity from the chapter's own witnesses (Clarke's camp-order table, Calvin on Judah's banner and on Reuben's fourth day, Henry on the identical gifts, on why the record repeats, on the sabbath and on the sin offering, Clarke on the sabbath and the Hebrew idiom for eleven) so that twelve identical offerings do not produce twelve identical write-ups.

Nine day entries graded B (18-23, 24-29, 30-35, 36-41, 42-47, 54-59, 60-65, 66-71, 78-83): each is carried by a witness block filed under a different verse of this chapter — Clarke's table at v14, Calvin at v12, Henry at v10, K&D at v11 — because the verses in the span itself carry no comment beyond the recitation of the gift. Faithful to the chapter's catena, not to the span's own slot. Graded A where the substance sits inside the span (12-17, 48-53, 72-77).

STRETCH flags of 10x-24x on the day pericopes and on 6-9 are false positives: synthesis-fidelity measures prose against the START-VERSE blob only, and these entries draw legitimately on chapter-level blocks (Henry's essay under key 1 covers vv.6-9; Clarke's table under key 14 covers all twelve days). ENTITIES flags Corinthians/James/Hebrews come from anchoring cross-references the witnesses themselves cite (Henry on 1 Cor 10:13, 1 Cor 15:23, Jas 2:1, Heb 6:10; Clarke on Heb 1:1-2).

Clarke's tabulated summary under key 14 misstates the peace offering as 'Five oxen, five rams, five he-goats, and five lambs'; the chapter text and Clarke's own running commentary give two oxen. Followed the text (two oxen) rather than the table.

Rewritten as 9 pericope entries tiling all 18 verses, following Clarke's own chapter outline at v1 (the lot of the half tribe 1-2; the case of Zelophehad's daughters 3-6; the borders 7-11, split here at 11 because Manasseh's towns in Issachar and Asher carry their own weight of comment; the Canaanites under tribute 12-13; the complaint 14-16, split per verse because Henry and Calvin each write an essay on it; Joshua's authorization 17-18).

Jamieson, Fausset and Brown blocks at vv.5 and 11 are scrape residue — a bare cross-reference to Deuteronomy 27:11 at v5, and a fragment on idol blocks and coloured stones at v11. Declared excluded_voices on the entries covering them; JFB is named nowhere in the chapter.

STRETCH 7.95x at 3-6 is a false positive: synthesis-fidelity measures the start-verse blob (81 words) but the pericope's source is the union of vv.3-6, 1231 usable words, giving about 0.5x. ENTITIES flags Genesis/Chronicles/Samuel come from anchoring cross-references the witnesses cite (Clarke on Gen 48:19-20, Henry on 1 Chron 7:21, Clarke on 1 Sam 28:7); Talmudic, Jerome and Zebulun are the witnesses' own vocabulary.

Calvin's block at v5 refuses every proposed solution to the ten portions and says the data are insufficient. Recorded as a third side in the debate rather than harmonised away, since he is explicitly contradicting the reckonings Gill, Clarke and Wesley give.

Every Jamieson, Fausset and Brown block in cow/genesis/24.json is scrape residue from Genesis 20-21: Abimelech and Abraham's equivocation (vv.6, 18), the naming and circumcision of Isaac (v.30), the weaning feast (v.36), the two peoples from a family brawl (v.42), the Beersheba wells (v.60), and the grove of tamarisks (v.66). Declared excluded_voices on every entry covering those keys; JFB is named nowhere in the chapter.

Rewritten as 21 pericope entries tiling all 67 verses: 1-4; 5-8; 9; 10-11; 12-14; 15-17; 18-21; 22-25; 26-27; 28-32; 33-38; 39-44; 45-49; 50-52; 53; 54-56; 57-58; 59-61; 62-63; 64-65; 66-67. The chapter is 31,571 usable source words across seven witnesses, so the grouping follows the narrative's own joints rather than thinness; the one genuinely repetitive stretch is the servant's retelling at 33-49, where Gill's comment is largely cross-references back to the first telling.

STRETCH 24.68x at 39-44 and 6.82x at 66-67 are false positives: synthesis-fidelity measures the start-verse blob (19 and 84 words) but the pericopes' sources are the unions of their spans (334 and 2637 usable words), giving about 1.4x and 0.22x.

'Abimelech' appears once in the 64-65 entry and is NOT drawn from the JFB residue: Ellicott's own note on the veil at v.65 says that after marriage it was seldom worn at this early period, 'and so both the Egyptians and Abimelech saw Sarah's beauty'. Flagged here because the residue in this chapter is Genesis 20 material, so the name could look like leakage on a later audit.

Numbers 32:41 source is ~1230 raw words but only ~250 are commentary (Gill, Clarke quoting Ainsworth, Ellicott). The rest is StudyLight page chrome: CSS blocks, inline JS, the site's book_data array, nav menus and a Cloudflare challenge snippet. Omitted silently and unnarrated, per the loop rules. Voices legitimately used at v41 also come from the Keil and Delitzsch block filed under key 40, which runs through vv.40-42.

Three Jamieson, Fausset and Brown blocks in this chapter carry foreign-passage material: v.5 holds JFB on the silver chargers and bowls of Numbers 7 plus his note on the flocks offered there; v.23 holds JFB on the laying of hands upon the Levites (Numbers 8); v.29 holds a fragment on carrying the covered furniture into the tabernacle (Numbers 4). All three declared as excluded_voices on the tags entries and omitted from the prose. JFB therefore appears in no verse of this chapter and is named nowhere.

Numbers 32:25 source blob ends with scrape residue from the site's pager ('Next: Numbers Chapter 33 Sacred Texts | Bible << Previous: John Gill's Exposition ...'). Not attributable to any witness, so not declarable as excluded_voices; simply omitted. It inflates the measured source for the thin test by roughly 35 words, which the 25-27 pericope still passes.

Five verses self-graded B, all for the same reason: a paragraph of the entry is the summary's own framing rather than a claim traceable to a named witness. v.3 — the contrast between the town-list as a claim and the same list as an inventory at the chapter's close. v.4 — the request set out as a syllogism whose flaw is in the conclusion (the criticism itself is Calvin's and Henry's). v.13 — what the recital means for the men listening, drawn from Ellicott's identification of the forty years as the fulfilment Moses himself announced. v.21 — that the tribes' own wording left the term of service conveniently open and Moses replaces it with one only God can close. v.22 — that the verse never treats the eastern country as second-best. No claim is put into any commentator's mouth in these; the grade marks framing weight, not invention.

synthesis-fidelity.py measures a pericope entry's expansion ratio against the KEY verse's source only, not the union of the span, so every ranged entry in this chapter reads as a stretch it is not. The STRETCH flag on v.18 (9.6x) is the clearest case: the 18-19 entry has 380 usable source words against 413 prose words, i.e. 1.09x. Same false positive shape at 9-11 (2.0x actual), 23-24 (1.18x), 25-27 (2.2x), 29-30 (1.3x), 31-32 (1.2x), 34-36 (0.70x), 37-38 (1.0x), 39-40 (1.18x). All judged false positives. Worth teaching the tool to sum the span when a range is declared.

ENTITIES flags judged false positives. v.23 'Cain' — Calvin cites Genesis 4:7 without naming him; the identification of who that sentence was spoken to is a factual gloss on his own citation, not a view attributed to him. v.34 'Amman' — Keil and Delitzsch write it, but the scrape has stripped the diacritic to 'Ammn' so the matcher misses it; 'Gideon' identifies the episode at Judges 8:11, which K&D cite by reference only. v.41 'Pileser' — Clarke's quoted text spells it 'Tiglath-Pilneser'; normalised. v.42 'Geshur' spells the source's 'Gesur' as 1 Chronicles 2:23 does, and 'Kanatha' transliterates the source's Greek. K&D's 'Jotan' was dropped from the prose rather than guessed at.

Numbers 32 repaired as 30 entries over 42 verses, using nine pericopes where the material is continuous or repetitive: 9-11 (the Eshcol recital), 18-19, 23-24, 25-27, 29-30, 31-32, 34-36 (Gad's town register), 37-38 (Reuben's), 39-40 (Machir). Spans tile the chapter exactly. Six entries take the thin exemption. The old prose carried all three audit defect shapes at once — 'The witnesses note' opening most sentences, the KJV verse re-quoted as the opening of all 42 entries, and the parenthesised slot-list ('walking the verse through: the X — gloss; the Y — gloss') in every verse. Regenerated rather than trimmed.

Cyril of Jerusalem blocks appear under acts 19 keys 1, 2, 5, 6, 10, 19 and 34, and every one of them is foreign-passage material: Antioch and Barnabas (Acts 11/13) at v.1, the garden tomb and the resurrection at v.2, baptism of water and Spirit at v.5, Eldad and Modad at v.6, the new Jerusalem at v.10, a doxology on the Spirit's works at v.19, and the devils confessing Christ at v.34. They read like consecutive paragraphs of the Catechetical Lectures distributed across the chapter by the scraper. All omitted silently and unnarrated; Cyril is named in no verse but 41. They could NOT be declared as excluded_voices because synthesis_qa.split_voices does not recognise 'Cyril of Jerusalem' as a block head, so the validator rejects the declaration.

The Cyril of Jerusalem block at acts 19:41 is the one legitimate one in the chapter: he quotes this very verse ('when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the Assembly') to argue that the word ecclesia covers a mob in a theatre as well as the Church, and builds the creed article on it. Used, and credited, at v.41 only. SourceIndex.ungrounded_voices confirms him grounded for the chapter.

Six Jamieson, Fausset and Brown blocks in this chapter are foreign-passage material, all of it from the passion and resurrection narratives: Clopas and Alpheus (John 19:25) at v.5; the sabbath eve and the breaking of legs (John 19:31) at vv.11 and 17; the rock-hewn tomb at v.23; Peter and John at the sepulchre at v.29; Mary and the two angels at v.35. All declared as excluded_voices on the tags entries and omitted from the prose. JFB is named nowhere in the chapter.

Two verses carry heavy StudyLight page chrome that inflates the measured source: v.21 is 8,295 raw words of which perhaps 2,600 are commentary (the rest is Chrysostom's homily plus a large block of CSS, inline JS, the site's book_data array and nav menus), and v.40 has the same tail. The fidelity tool therefore reports v.21 at 0.08x, which is an artefact of the chrome rather than a real compression. Same shape as the numbers 32:41 defect noted 2026-08-15.

Four verses self-graded B, each for the same reason: one closing paragraph of the entry is the summary's own framing rather than a claim traceable to a named witness. v.7 — the number twelve weighed against what these men had just confessed not to know. v.28 — that the shout answers nothing in what Demetrius reported Paul as saying. v.36 — that the recorder's counsel against haste is good whatever the creed of the man giving it. v.39 — that he has sorted a religious emergency into two ordinary categories with a venue for each. No claim is put into any commentator's mouth; the grade marks framing weight. Every other verse graded A, and the chapter's expansion ratios are unusually low (median well under 0.5x) because the sources are very full.

Five ENTITIES flags judged false positives. v.11 'Maccabees' — Robertson cites 'III Macc. 3:7', which the matcher does not expand. v.17 'Nazianzus' — Clarke spells it 'Nazianzen'; the prose was changed to match his spelling, so this flag should clear on the next run. v.19 'Eustathius' — Barnes cites him as 'Eustha. ad Homer. Odys.'; the name was expanded. v.24 'Hindu' — Ellicott writes 'Hindoo idol'; spelling normalised. v.29 'Hermae' — Ellicott writes 'Hermae-busts' with a ligature the scrape mangles. None introduces a claim absent from the source.

acts 19 repaired as 41 entries, one per verse — no pericopes, because every verse in this chapter draws distinct comment from six to nine witnesses, and grouping would have discarded material rather than avoided templating. Only v.7 (134 usable source words) took the thin exemption. The old prose carried all three audit defect shapes: 'The witnesses note' opening most sentences, the full KJV verse in quotes at the head of all 41 entries, and near-duplicate sentences restating the same point three or four times. Regenerated throughout. John Chrysostom's homily block sits under key 8 but covers vv.8-40, and is drawn on at vv.8, 13, 21, 24, 25 and 26.

FIXED 2026-08-15: the pericope expansion-ratio defect reported from the numbers 32 run is closed. QA.span_source_text/span_keys now answer 'what does this entry stand on', and both synthesis-fidelity.py and the expansion that backfill-synthesis-qa.py stamps go through them, so a ranged entry is measured against the union of its span — the same span the thin exemption has always summed. All 50 ranged entries in the four chapters that use ranges (genesis/24, joshua/17, numbers/7, numbers/32) were re-stamped with the real numbers using the new --keep-generated flag, which preserves qa.generated because a re-measurement is not a regeneration. 14 false STRETCH flags disappeared (worst: numbers 7:6 at a reported 24.12x, really 0.93x; genesis 24:39 at 24.68x, really 1.4x; numbers 32:18 at 9.6x, really 1.09x). Verified against a HEAD worktree that non-ranged chapters are byte-identical. Left deliberately unchanged: the ratio still counts scrape residue in the denominator, which understates it on chrome-heavy verses but errs toward not flagging.

Five Jamieson, Fausset and Brown blocks in this chapter are foreign-passage material and were declared as excluded_voices on the entries covering them: v.5 holds JFB on the proclamation of the divine name at Exodus 34; vv.11, 17, 23 and 29 all carry the same fragment about bowing the head to royalty in the East. JFB is named nowhere in the prose. The v.47 blob also ends in a long tail of StudyLight page chrome (CSS, inline JS, the site's book_data array), which inflates its measured source from ~350 real words to 1,379.

Ellicott's note on leviticus 11:44 introduces the quotation 'be ye holy, for I am holy' with 'the Apostle Paul uses the same admonition' and then quotes 1 Peter 1:15-16. The attribution is wrong in the source. The prose credits it to 'the apostle' without naming him and anchors 1 Peter 1:15, so the error is neither reproduced nor silently corrected into a claim Ellicott did not make.

Three ENTITIES flags judged false positives, all spelling normalisations of the source's older forms: v.17 'Delft' (Gill writes 'the city of Delf in Holland'), v.20 'Libyans' (Wesley writes 'Lybians'), v.29 'Nile' (Keil and Delitzsch write 'lacerta Nilotica', which the matcher does not expand). None introduces a claim absent from the source.

One entry self-graded B: the 39-40 pericope, whose closing paragraph sets the chapter's remediable ceremonial defilement (water, a broken pot, the coming of evening) against the excision reserved for deliberate contempt. The excision itself is Ellicott's and Wesley's point on this verse; the contrast drawn across the whole chapter is the summary's own framing. Every other entry graded A. Expansion ratios run 0.14x-0.73x — heavy distillation throughout, since the sources here are enormous and largely natural-history digression.

leviticus 11 repaired as 15 entries over 47 verses, using pericopes throughout because this is a register chapter of exactly the shape the rule was written for: vv.4-7 repeat one formula word for word, vv.10-12 repeat 'abomination' three times, and the bird, insect and creeping-thing lists are catalogues. Spans: 1-2, 3, 4-8, 9-12, 13-16, 17-19, 20-23, 24-28, 29-31, 32-35, 36-38, 39-40, 41-43, 44-45, 46-47; they tile the chapter exactly. No thin exemptions — every span is richly sourced. Verse 3 kept its own entry because the two marks of the clean beast draw distinct comment from six witnesses. The old prose carried all three audit defect shapes. The chapter's real spine is a running disagreement about WHY the law exists: Clarke argues hard for a hygienic purpose and Henry, Gill and Wesley allow it a place, while Calvin refuses it three separate times in the sharpest language in the chapter ('those who imagine that God here had regard to their health... pervert by their vain speculation the whole force and utility of this law'), and Wesley finally says there was no real uncleanness in the creatures at all. That division is recorded as a debate on vv.1-2 and again on vv.44-45.

Every Jamieson, Fausset and Brown block in this chapter is foreign material: v.12 'Here are given special directions for the observance.' (a stray fragment), v.18 'All the preceding directions were communicated through the elders...' (belongs to a narrative passage, not to the cherubim), v.30 'literally, a great rabble...' (the mixed multitude of Exodus 12:38). All three omitted from the prose and declared as excluded_voices on entries 12, 18 and 30. JFB is named nowhere in the chapter.

Ellicott's block under key 40 is almost entirely StudyLight page chrome — nav menus, CSS, JS, the book_data array. The only usable sentence is his one-line cross-reference back to v.9. Gill's block under key 40 also ends in site navigation residue. Both omitted; Ellicott is therefore not named in entry 40.

Rewritten with six ranged entries (12-15, 19-20, 26-28, 32-33, 34-36, 37-38) plus one thin entry (25). The old chapter wrote all 40 verses to ~330-430 words each, which forced heavy padding on verses whose only witness is a one-line Gill gloss (v.13 45 words, v.14 39, v.28 31, v.35 95). Grouping them by what the witnesses actually treat as one unit — the ark's carrying gear, the cherubim's placement and posture, the table's rings and staves, the branches and their almond cups, the shaft and its junctions, the lamps and their tongs — gives each entry real material. Spans tile the chapter exactly.

Three entries graded B. v.21: the closing paragraph gathers the sprinkled blood (Clarke on v.17), the voice from between the cherubim (Ellicott/K&D on v.22) and the title 'ark of the testimony' into one summary — every element is in the chapter's sources, but the synthesis of them is mine. v.24: the closing paragraph infers that ark and table were built to one specification so a worshipper outside the veil could know both were of one design; the witnesses state the parallel construction but draw no such inference. vv.26-28: the closing paragraph applies the ark's 'carried, never handled' rule to the table; Ellicott states that principle only of the ark (v.15).

Four ENTITIES flags judged false positives. 'Noah' at v.10 and v.17 glosses Genesis 6:14, which Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch both cite by chapter and verse (tebah as against aron; kaphar as 'to pitch'). 'Englished' at v.29 is an ordinary English verb, not a proper noun. 'Ephesus' at v.40 names the city of the silver shrines for Diana that Clarke cites from Acts 19:24 — a geographic gloss on his own citation, not a view attributed to him.

Driver/environment bug worth fixing: in the scheduled CCR container the repo is checked out with a DETACHED HEAD. synthesis-loop.py push_chapter runs 'git push -u origin master', which in that state pushes the stale local branch 'master' rather than HEAD, so every attempt is rejected as non-fast-forward and finish reports 'push rejected four times' (exit 4) even though the commit is sound and 'git push origin HEAD:master' would fast-forward. Worked around by hand this run: git checkout -B master <commit>, git reset --mixed origin/master, re-run finish --push. Suggested fix: push HEAD:master, or refuse to start when HEAD is detached.
